llm.summary: The skill claims full, multi‑platform autoposting and video generation but the included code only implements posting to X (Twitter/X) and thread generation — requested credentials and feature claims are disproportionate to the actual implementation.

dimensions.detail: The skill's name/description and SKILL.md promise posting to X, Instagram, YouTube, and Meta plus HTML→video generation and scheduling. The code bundle only contains X-focused scripts (x_poster.py, x_thread_generator.py, formatter.py). There are no Instagram/Meta/YouTube posting scripts or any HTML→video pipeline code. Requesting multi‑platform support in the manifest/instructions is inconsistent with the actual files.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Runtime instructions ask the agent to run autonomously, read a content DB (data/*.csv), post answers as comments, and generate videos via HTML→PNG→MP4 with music and watermarking. The code reads data/questions.csv and formats/posts tweets and threads, and can upload media to X; it does not implement video generation, GitHub Actions scheduling, or posting to IG/Meta/YouTube. The SKILL.md therefore overclaims capabilities and could mislead a user into supplying extra assets/credentials they are not needed for the provided code.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No install spec is present (instruction-only + included scripts). Nothing is downloaded or executed via a remote URL during install. This is lower risk compared to remote installs; files are local in the package for review.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md asks for many environment variables (X_*, IG_*, META_*) for multiple platforms. The included Python code reads only X_* variables (tweepy usage). Requiring Instagram and Meta tokens in instructions but not using them in code is disproportionate and confusing — supplying those tokens would grant broader access than the code actually needs, increasing risk if the package is later extended or modified.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always:false (default) is set, so the skill is not force‑included, but model invocation is allowed (normal). Because the skill is intended to autonomously post, providing posting credentials enables the agent to act without manual confirmation. This combination (autonomous posting capability + requested posting tokens) raises operational risk (accidental or unwanted posts) even though it does not by itself indicate malicious intent.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This package is suspiciously overpromising: it claims multi‑platform autoposting and video generation, but the shipped code only implements posting to X and thread generation. Before installing or adding credentials: (1) Do not provide Instagram/Meta/YouTube tokens until you confirm corresponding code exists. (2) Review the repository/homepage/source (the skill's source is 'unknown' here); prefer packages with an auditable public repo. (3) If you want to test, use a throwaway/test social account and limited-scope app tokens so accidental posts don't affect real accounts. (4) If you expect video generation or IG/Meta posting, request the missing implementation from the author or inspect updates; otherwise treat the SKILL.md claims as inaccurate. (5) Consider running the scripts locally in dry‑run mode (instrument tweepy calls or mock env vars) to verify what the agent will actually do.
